raw_comment: This graph was created to reveal how calorie count and portion sizes have grown over the years. Across the board, it can be seen that even if portion sizes changed minimally, the calorie count went up. This can especially be seen in desserts, where the portion size went up by some but the calorie count nearly doubled. This graph says a lot about modern day food and how Americans eat. We have a culture based around fast food, which has tightened its grip over us in the past half century and in doing so has also lead to an increase in the consumption of calories. This ever-growing epidemic is what has led to America’s two biggest problems, diabetes and heart disease, and is a predicament that needs to be controlled before it gets completely out of control. From a very young age, American children are institutionalized to like fast food because companies market such food towards them, and this begins the cycle of addiction and consumption that leads to these problems. Promoting healthier eating from a young age would be one thing that could help to break such a cycle. In all, these graphs are a great demonstration of how unhealthy food has become.

The grams are the lowest on the side dishes and the highest on the entrees. I wonder why the calories and grams went up when the years passed, did they add those things on purpose? I also wonder if you added data for three more years if the numbers would continue to increase? Another wondering is if you decrease the portion size if the calorie count would go up, down, or stay the same? In this graph, they took the calories and portion grams from only fast food places. If you continue to do the graph, you could have calories up too 1,000 calories in all sorts of foods and desserts. If people don’t care or pay attention to the number of calories that they are eating, they are going to be in for a surprise.

I wonder if the serving sizes and calories of various foods and restaurants will continue to increase perpetually. If so, Americans should be extremely concerned about their health and should avoid eating out as much as possible. The only way to avoid complicated health issues that are affecting people all over the country, such as obesity, are to bring those serving sizes and calories back down. Thanks to all students who responded.  Love the catchy headlines that capture the main ideas of the map:  “Bigger? Yes. Better? Not So Much.” by Ms. Mangold’s 3-5 grade at Red Fox Community School, Dorset, VT, “The Graph Gets Wider Just Like Americans” by Barbra of NSHS, and “Catching Calories, An American Dream” by Mrs. Lane’s class at North Star Elementary School, Salt Lake City, Utah, and “Calorie Count Continues to Climb” by Team Teddy at Eden Prairie High School. 

You can continue to post responses.  Please check back tomorrow --  Thursday afternoon, October 17 to see the Reveal with a link to the original New York Times article, some questions about the graphs, and a few Stat Nuggets.
 
The next graph will be released tomorrow -- THURSDAY, OCTOBER 17, with moderation on WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 23.  You may respond before, during, or after the live moderation by going to ““What's Going On In This Graph?”  The topic --  the drop in pet euthanasia.  Also, you can view the webinar with teachers and students discussing how to learn from graphs using The New York Times.  Go tohttps://webinars.on24.com/nyt/Graphs?partnerref=OnDemand.
.
Signing off – Sharon Hessney of Boston, who has never thought that one eats fast food to be healthy – it just tastes good, and Vicki Greenberg of Atlanta, who simply cannot refuse a good fast food double cheeseburger.

raw_comment:
Part 2-
I wonder if the serving sizes and calories of various foods and restaurants will continue to increase perpetually. If so, Americans should be extremely concerned about their health and should avoid eating out as much as possible. The size of fast food servings has been increased to accommodate the growing size of Americans. The only way to avoid complicated health issues that are affecting people all over the country, such as obesity, are to bring those serving sizes and calories back down. Even better, people should ensure that the number of times they eat at fast food places is as minimal as possible in order to avoid the temptations of ordering high-calorie desserts and burgers. If the people in the U.S. want to decrease the levels of health problems such as diabetes, high cholesterol, and obesity in their country, they must restore the lower-calorie foods to restaurants or completely avoid eating at fast food places.

Red Fox Community School, Dorset, Vermont 3-5th Grade

Headline: "Bigger, Yes, Better, Not So Much"
We noticed that the numbers increased every year which is not good. We also noticed that the sides are closer to even calorie amounts and portion size, while the entrees and desserts go up, and have much higher calorie counts than portion size.
We think there needs to be better ingredients and healthier choices, rather than high calorie options.
Check your sources, know where your food comes from and don't buy food in plastic or cellophane containers.

raw_comment:
As the description of the graph states, the portion size and calorie count increase significantly over the years. This could be due to a lot of things, such as globalization of large corporations, catering to the "growing" size of our populations, and other factors. The growing size of the fast food industry and competition among the corporations means that the food they serve could go in either direction in terms of quality. In an ideal society, close competition in the marketplace would lead to the competitors striving to attract more customers with higher quality items, however quite the opposite is true in the real world. Modern corporations reach for quantity over quality and market lies through heavy advertisement to drill their food ideas into the minds of the public. The graph could show the loss of quality in food through the use of lower quality and higher calorie items that contain sugars, sodium, fats, and preservatives so that the fast food joints could sell more food for less cost to the company. 
The next thing this graph could show is how corporations are catering to the "growing" size of our populations. In the U.S., we are facing an epidemic of obesity, and fast food corporations have fallen under the limelight of blame in past years for this issue. This catering to size can be seen in fast food history, such as the supersize craze of the early 1990's to the mid 2000's. The graph shows the year in 1991 right before McDonald's dropped the idea.

raw_comment:
In this graph, I notice how the proportions and calorie count of entrees, sides, and desserts have increased over 30 years. I was particularly shocked when I saw the increase of the calorie count of desserts. In 1986, the amount of calories in desserts was only 234 while the calorie count now is 420. The calorie count now is almost twice the number of calories than in 1986. From this graph, I can see that Americans slowly eat more than before which has benefits less people suffering from hunger, but can also lead to being overweight.

       One thing I wonder about this graph is if the serving size will continue increasing. If the number of calories and proportions of these foods now are already almost 2 times the amount as 1986 and continues increasing, in the future, the serving size might become 3 or even 4 times the amount. 

     If this trend keeps continuing, a person might be in danger by eating too much calories per day. To stop this, the fast food restaurants should make the foods healthier. There are many other foods that can be healthier substitutes of the foods served in fast food restaurant. By making the foods heathier Americans can eat more without gaining as much weight.
